guide.title: Getting the custom firmware onto a box
guide.intro: This is how a box that still runs the original firmware gets the custom firmware. The way depends on the chip of the box (<identify>identify the box version</identify>). teddyCloud's CFW support has to be switched on for it.

cc3200.cardZip: A ready SD card content does steps 3 to 6 too (bootloader, firmware, setup page, server): <card>make the SD card zip</card>.
cc3200.step1: The box must already run with teddyCloud and have the HackieboxNG SD bootloader. See <setup>Add Toniebox</setup> (CC3200) for how to do that.
cc3200.step2: Take the release package of the custom firmware (toniebox-cfw-….zip), the same one you load into the library below, and unpack it on your computer.
cc3200.step3: The custom firmware needs the adapted HackieboxNG bootloader with trial start and automatic return on updates. It is in the package as cc3200/ngbootloader.bin: copy it over /revvox/boot/ngbootloader.bin on the SD card.
cc3200.step4: Copy to the SD card: cc3200/ng-cfw.bin to /revvox/boot/ng-cfw1.bin and setup.htm to /cfw/setup.htm.
cc3200.step5: Enter the server in /cfw/config.txt: host={{host}} (and port= if needed). It can be changed later on the setup page of the box too.
cc3200.step6: In /revvox/boot/ngCfg.json set "activeImg": "cfw1" and "stateFile": "/revvox/boot/ngstate.bin" under general. The original firmware stays: with the previous activeImg (usually "ofw1") the box starts as before.
cc3200.step7: Put the card back and start the box. It reports to teddyCloud with the custom firmware and shows up here under "Boxes". All further updates come through this page.
cc3200.title: Toniebox with CC3200 chip (SD card)

esp32.title: Toniebox with ESP32 chip (through teddyCloud)
esp32.step1: The box must run the original firmware patched for teddyCloud, see <setup>Add Toniebox</setup> (ESP32). Keep the flash dump made there in a safe place.
esp32.step2: Load the flash dump of the original firmware into the library below (the patches for teddyCloud are explained at the upload). With it the box can go back to the original firmware at any time.
esp32.step3: Load the release package of the custom firmware (toniebox-cfw-….zip) into the library below.
esp32.step4: Under "Boxes" the box is listed as "Original firmware / unknown". Assign the ESP32 image to it.
esp32.step5: Restart the box. At its update check it downloads the image once, with this server ({{host}}) already set, writes it into the free slot and starts the custom firmware. The box does not have to be opened.
esp32.step6: Back to the original firmware: assign the image of the original firmware to the box. It installs it at its next update check.

controls.title: Using a box with the custom firmware
controls.intro: Only the custom firmware has these gestures and functions; the original firmware does not know them.

restart.title: Slap upside down: start over
restart.text: Turn the box upside down (ears facing down) and slap it on the side: playback jumps back to the beginning of the figure, with the "chapter back" sound. With shuffle, a new random order starts. In the original firmware, a slap on the upside-down box only moves one chapter. Handy for audio books and figures with many chapters. The slap lock stops this gesture too.

bothEars.title: Both ears briefly: switch off
bothEars.text: Press both ears together and let go within 2 s: the LED blinks lilac once, the box keeps the position and switches off at once, even with a figure on it. Holding longer works as before (5 s: setup mode, 10 s upside down: restart). Can be switched off in the box settings.

anyTag.title: Any NFC tag as a figure
anyTag.text: Besides real Tonies, any ISO 15693 NFC tag works (e.g. stickers or cards). The box reads only its ID and never writes to it. Assign its content in teddyCloud like for any Tonie.

event.title: Event tags
event.text: An event tag plays nothing; it changes the next figure (placed within 60 s) or the box. Set it up in the Tonie's edit dialog. Confirmation: five turquoise blinks = switched on, five lilac blinks = switched off. While an event tag "with the ears" is on the box, the ears set the volume limit or the LED; holding one ear for 3 s switches between the two.

locks.title: Locks
locks.text: Per box or per figure: slap lock (changing chapters, the upside-down slap included), tilt lock (winding) and volume lock (short ear press). A locked gesture does nothing at all: no sound, no blink.

faq.answer: To force an update, perform a freshness check on your Toniebox. Press and hold one of the ears for approximately 3 seconds until you hear a sound. Wait until a second sound confirms the completion of the update.
faq.question: How can I force an update of a Tonie after assigning new content in TeddyCloud?

faq.answer: Use the Audioencoder tool and add up to 99 audio files. Each file will be assigned its own track in the created TAF file.
faq.question: How can I create a multi-track TAF file?

faq.answer: You can add up to 16 Tonieboxes to a single TeddyCloud instance.
faq.question: How many Tonieboxes can I add to a TeddyCloud instance?

faq.answer: Place the tag on a connected Toniebox. It will automatically be added to your Tonies in TeddyCloud. If you have many unknown tags, you can filter for the last played tags or open the Toniebox management page and click on the last played tag.
faq.question: How can I add a new tag to TeddyCloud?

faq.answer: The easiest way to remove a tag is to hide it. Open the information modal for the tag you want to remove and click the 'Hide' button. The tag will remain hidden until it is placed on a Toniebox again. Alternatively, if you have access to the SD cards of all connected Tonieboxes, you can delete the tag physically by removing the corresponding content folder for that tag on each box and then removing it in TeddyCloud content view.
faq.question: How can I remove a tag from my TeddyCloud?

faq.answer: Set up a separate content directory for each Toniebox in the Toniebox management settings. Afterward, the Tonies overview will feature a dropdown menu in the top right corner where you can choose between different content directories. You don't need to assign a unique content directory to each box; boxes with the same content directory will be grouped together in the Tonies overview.
faq.question: How can I manage different contents for a tag on different Tonieboxes?

faq.answer: Perform a freshness check on that Toniebox. This will re-add all tags that have ever been placed on the box (and are not deleted) to TeddyCloud. Original Tonies need to be placed at least once to get the cloud authentication and download their linked content to TeddyCloud.
faq.question: Why is the Tonies overview empty after adding a new content directory to a box?

faq.answer: Ensure that the 'nocloud' flag is set to true and verify that no one has secretly placed another tag on the box.
faq.question: Why does my tag with custom content always start from the beginning instead of the last played position?

faq.answer: Ensure the following settings are enabled: 'Cache Content' and 'Dump rUID/auth'. We also recommend enabling 'Cache to library'.
faq.question: Why isn't the content of my tags cached to TeddyCloud?

faq.answer: Make sure you're using the correct type of tag. Only original NSP SLIX-L tags are generally compatible. You will find more information about this in the forum. If you have the CC3200 version of the Toniebox, you can enable other RFID tags as well. Check the wiki for more details. Additionally, ensure there is a certain distance between the tag and the Toniebox (at least 2-3mm) as a directly placed RFID tag won't work properly.

CH341AProgrammer.flashMemoryDumpText3: When ready, plug the CH341A into the USB port on your computer. The Toniebox light should turn solid green. If it flickers, the clamp may not be positioned well. Disconnect the CH341A, adjust the clamp, and try again to ensure a good connection.
CH341AProgrammer.flashMemoryDumpText4: Once the LED is steady green, the connection is good. Open a terminal on your computer and type the following commands:
CH341AProgrammer.flashMemoryDumpText5: Repeat this process at least three times.
CH341AProgrammer.flashMemoryDumpText6: After three reads, compare all dumps to confirm consistency.
CH341AProgrammer.flashMemoryDumpText7: Once you confirm that all versions are consistent, proceed with certificate extraction.
CH341AProgrammer.flashMemoryDumpText8: Remove the CH341A from the USB port and remove the clamp to avoid potential shorts or issues if the clamp accidentally moves.
CH341AProgrammer.prep1: Obtain a CH341A programmer (only purchase the black version with a gold line and rounded edges).
CH341AProgrammer.prep2: Trim the plastic on the CH341A clamp if necessary, so it can fit onto the IS25LP032D Flash memory.
CH341AProgrammer.prep3: Ensure both the PCB and the battery are disconnected.
CH341AProgrammer.prep4: Connect the CH341A to the computer and confirm it is recognized. You can do this as follows:
CH341AProgrammer.prepConclusions1: If the output differs, the small bridge between pins 1 and 2 on the CH341A may not be set. Once confirmed, unplug the CH341A from the USB port. This check ensures everything is connected correctly.
CH341AProgrammer.prepConclusions2: Make sure the SOP8 module in the CH341A kit and the clamp are connected as shown in the picture.
CH341AProgrammer.prepConclusions3: Only when preparations are complete can we proceed with the extraction process.

fields.claimed: Whether this Tonie has been claimed (true/false).

fields.picture: The image path or URL assigned to the Tonie.
fields.ruid: The reversed UID of the Tonie in lowercase without colons (:).
fields.series: The series name of the Tonie.
fields.source: The assigned source of the Tonie (taf, tap, or stream).
fields.track: Search for an exact track name in the Tonie.
fields.trackcount: The number of tracks in the Tonie.
fields.tracks: An array of track names in the Tonie.
fields.trackseconds: An array with the start position in seconds of each track in the Tonie.
fields.tracksecondscount: The number of track start positions in the Tonie.
fields.uid: The UID (unique identifier) of the Tonie.

customFilterHelp.intro: Use the Custom Filter to filter Tonies with logical expressions and field-specific conditions.

syntaxExamples.and: Filters Tonies where series is 'Pixi' AND the Tonie is valid.
syntaxExamples.combined: Filters Tonies that are live, have cloud access, German language and unique in series.
syntaxExamples.endswith: Filters Tonies where the field ends with the given value.
syntaxExamples.inList: Filters Tonies where the field matches any of the given values.
syntaxExamples.isEmpty: Filters Tonies where the field is empty.
syntaxExamples.isNotEmpty: Filters Tonies where the field is not empty.
syntaxExamples.negation: Filters Tonies that have cloud access.
syntaxExamples.notInList: Filters Tonies where the field matches none of the given values.
syntaxExamples.or: Filters Tonies with either German or French language.
syntaxExamples.series: Filters Tonies where the series is 'Pixi'.
syntaxExamples.startswith: Filters Tonies where the field starts with the given value.
syntaxExamples.title: Syntax Examples
syntaxExamples.trackSecondsCountCompare: Filter by the number of track start positions
syntaxExamples.trackSecondsCountEqualsTrackCount: Filter for tonies where length of track start position array equals number of tracks
syntaxExamples.trackSecondsCountNotEqualsTrackCount: Filter for tonies where length of track start position array does not equal number of tracks
syntaxExamples.tracksRegex: Filter tracks using a regex pattern
syntaxExamples.unique: Filters Tonies that are the only one in their series.

tips.caseSensitive: Field names are case-sensitive; use lowercase exactly as shown.
tips.combine: Combine multiple conditions with AND / OR, and negate with !.
